Oldenborn.

“You are not an elf. You are the memory of a place that learned to walk again.”

Dream-Flesh. You do not sleep. When you rest, you drift into Yesod—symbolic memory-space—unless you choose otherwise. You are immune to magical sleep, and you can always tell when a dream, illusion, or constructed reality is present.

Old Memory, Old Paths. You reroll the lowest die on checks to interpret ruins, follow ley-lines, identify altered terrain, and sense metaphysical instability. You always know if a place feels remembered, abandoned, or contested (the GM answers vaguely).

Veil-Sight. You perceive the presence of spirits, ghosts, Spark echoes, and noospheric constructs. This grants awareness, not perfect sight.

You Are Remembered. When you first meet a community, the GM chooses (or rolls) whether you are met with reverence, fear, or familiarity. It’s never neutral.

Normalized Heritage. This item preserves the original UUID for Rustlander Scavenger while converting it from a species-root into an Oldenborn heritage. Renamed to Rustland Scavenger to match v2 canon.

“Yesod fell. The world remembered old names. You answered.”

Oldenborn (Rustland Scavenger). Your place-soul is a dead city that refused to finish dying. You are the genius loci of collapsed transit hubs, rebar graveyards, and the smell of old oil. Every ruin you walk into recognizes you on arrival and, quietly, offers you what’s left.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Fey, Rustland).
  • Size. Medium.
  • Speed. 6 squares
  • attributes. Oldenborn does not grant fixed attribute bonuses; your background handles increases. Your heritage leans toward MND (Mind) or INTR (Intrigue) in fiction and mechanics via Tier powers.

Oldenborn Core

At character creation, you gain Old Memory, Old Flesh (Dream-Flesh, Old Paths, Veil-Sight, You Are Remembered).

Rustland Scavenger Traits

  • Toxic Lung Filters. reroll-lowest on checks against inhaled toxins, smoke, and industrial residue. You can function for up to 1 hour in atmospheres that would hospitalize a normal Medium creature.
  • Urban Scrounger. You gain a skill rank with the Investigation skill. You can always tell which structure in a ruin is load-bearing, which doorway is the real exit, and which pile of junk has something useful in it.
  • Patch & Repurpose. During a Soma Break spent in a ruin or wreckage hex, you can recover one expended consumable (bandage, filter, torch, ration) per Soma Break by scavenging.
  • Ruin Sense. You read marketplaces, ruins, and hex politics at a glance and can always tell what the last three meaningful events were in a trade hub.

Domain Edge

  • Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +20 Intrigue marks and +20 Economy marks at campaign start.

description.value:
⚔ AURABLADE — MECHANICAL CORE (PHASE 1.5)

Emotion is not flavor text.
Emotion is a resource.

🔥 Burn — What It Is (Plainly)

Burn represents emotional overextension:

  • Adrenaline overload

  • Suppressed fear

  • Moral fixation

  • Spiritual strain

Burn is not a die pool.
Burn is a state track that unlocks power and risk.

You do not “spend” Burn.
You enter Burn states, and the game responds.

🔥 How You Gain Burn (Concrete Triggers)

You gain 1 Burn when any one of the following occurs:

Universal Burn Triggers

  • You hit with an attack granted or enhanced by your Aura

  • You force a defense check using an Aura feature

  • You escalate without pause (GM-flagged high-risk continuation)

  • You remain in the same Aura for too long without stabilizing

⚠️ Limit:
You bank at most 2 Burn a round from landed hits; each Aura action adds 1, and a subclass may say otherwise.

Burn rewards commitment, not spam.

🔥 Burn States (Explicit Bands)

Burn is divided into three states.

🔹 Burn 0–1 — Controlled

You are emotionally steady.

  • You gain only passive Aura benefits

  • No backlash risk

  • No forced effects

This is the safe state.

🔸 Burn 2–3 — Engaged

Your emotion is active and visible.

At this state:

  • Your Aura unlocks standard combat riders

  • Your abilities gain explicit mechanical effects

  • You may choose to push harder

This is the intended combat state.

🔥 Burn 4+ — Overheated

You are exceeding safe emotional limits.

At this state:

  • Aura effects intensify

  • GM is authorized to:

    • Trigger backlash

    • Apply collateral

    • Force Aura collapse on a bad roll or narrative beat

This is the danger state.

🔥 What Happens at Backlash (Clear, Bounded)

When backlash triggers (GM discretion or subclass feature):

One of the following occurs (GM chooses or rolls):

  • You take psychic or sephirotic damage

  • You suffer roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on your next attack or save

  • Your Aura collapses (you drop to Burn 0)

  • A narrative consequence occurs (fear, escalation, attention)

Aurablades are not punished randomly.
They are punished predictably.

💠 AURA STATES — EXPLICIT MECHANICAL EFFECTS

Each Aura grants:

  • A passive effect

  • Engaged Burn effects

  • Overheated Burn effects

These are not manifestations.
They are combat permissions.

🔥 FURY — Escalation & Force

Theme: Press harder. Break lines.

Passive (Always On)

  • +1 bonus to damage rolls with melee weapon attacks

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

When you hit with a melee attack:

  • Deal +tier damage

  • You may push the target 1 square or cleave a second creature within reach (once per turn)

You may also:

  • Ignore roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on one attack per turn

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

When you hit:

  • Target must succeed on a Violence defense or be knocked prone

  • Your attacks deny reactions until the start of your next turn

⚠️ Risk:

  • On a missed attack, GM may trigger backlash

Fury trades control for dominance.

🛡 RESOLVE — Defense & Refusal

Theme: Stand firm. Make removal expensive.

Passive (Always On)

  • +1 bonus to Guard while you have not moved this turn

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

You may:

  • Halve the next hit you take before the start of your next turn

  • Ignore forced movement up to 2 squares

Additionally:

  • Reaction strikes against you roll 3d10 and keep the lowest 2

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

You may:

  • Automatically succeed on one Violence, Body, or Intrigue check per round

  • Lock your position: enemies cannot move you at all

⚠️ Risk:

  • When damage is fully negated, backlash may occur

Resolve dares the world to try harder.

🤍 MERCY — Protection & Restraint

Theme: Prevent loss. Redirect harm.

Passive (Always On)

  • You may choose to deal nonlethal damage without penalty

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

Once per round, when an ally within 2 squares takes damage:

  • Reduce that damage by tier

  • You may redirect it to yourself

You may also:

  • Automatically stabilize a creature you touch

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

You may:

  • Prevent an ally from dropping below 1 Integrity (once per round)

  • Convert a failed Last Stand check into a success

⚠️ Risk:

  • Preventing death may trigger backlash or Aura collapse

Mercy delays consequences — it does not erase them.

🕳 DREAD — Suppression & Collapse

Theme: Remove hope. End momentum.

Passive (Always On)

  • Enemies within 1 square suffer roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on fear and nerve checks (GM adjudication)

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

On hit:

  • Target must make a Soul defense or be Shaken until the end of its next turn

  • Target cannot take reactions

You may also:

  • Suppress one buff or inspiration effect (GM adjudication)

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

When you hit:

  • Target suffers roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on all saves until the start of your next turn

  • Nearby enemies must make a defense check or hesitate (lose movement or reactions)

⚠️ Risk:

  • Collateral fear or narrative fallout is likely

Dread does not kill bodies.
It kills belief.

🔄 Changing Aura (Explicit Rule)

You may change your Aura:

  • As a bonus action

  • Or as part of a Soma Break or narrative reset

Changing Aura:

  • Costs 1 Burn

  • Does not clear Burn; Stabilize or Meditate for that

Frequent swapping = control
Deep commitment = power

🧠 How Players Should Think About Aurablade

Ask yourself every turn:

  • “Do I escalate — or stabilize?”

  • “Can I afford another Burn?”

  • “What happens if this goes wrong?”

Aurablades are not forgiving.

They are honest.

Open the Aurablade action dialog. Available options depend on your current Aura and Burn band.

“Emotion sharpens faster than steel.”

Aura States (Fury, Resolve, Mercy, Dread) shape a luminous blade. Spending power builds Burn; at high Burn you gain potency and risk backlash.

Entropy has a shape. I cut along it.

Mode: Edge-walker

Void Edge Aurablades cut along the seams of decay. The doctrine suppresses what enemies rely on — buffs, banked rerolls, nerve — and propagates dread into the spaces between people. Played as the operative whose presence makes hope harder to organize.

Doctrine Features

  • Level 3 — Null Field. Your blade suppresses their edge. When you hit at Burn 1+, suppress one of the following until the end of the target's next turn: reroll-lowest on attacks, bonus damage, or fear or inspiration effects. At Burn 3+ the target also loses one reaction.
  • Level 6 — Silence of Will. You break focus. Targets you hit roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on Clarity hold checks and cannot benefit from rallying or command effects. At Burn 3+, failing a Clarity hold also causes Burn-like fatigue (GM narrative).
  • Level 10 — Dread Cut. Fear propagates. When you hit at Burn 2+, the target saves or is Shaken; nearby enemies save or suffer hesitation (lose movement or reactions). At Burn 4+ fear spreads automatically to one additional creature.
  • Level 14 — Emotional Erasure. Once per round when you hit, remove one beneficial emotional, nerve, or inspiration effect from the target. Bypasses resistance tied to hope or courage. At Burn 4+ the effect cannot be reapplied for 1 round.
  • Level 18 — Final Quiet (Capstone). Once per Soma Break, create a 6 squares zone for 1 minute: nerve cannot rise, inspiration fails, hope or courage buffs do not apply, enemies roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on checks vs fear. Afterward your Burn drops to 0.

“The dead cities are not silent. They are mid-sentence.”

Ruin-Sense. When you spend 10 minutes examining a broken or ruined object, you can ask the GM one of: What was its last use? Who broke it? What does it still want? The answer is at least one truth.

Scavenger’s Eye (1/Soma Break). Spend 10 minutes searching a rubble pile, gutted building, or wreckage of any kind. You recover one minor useful item — the GM picks from a short list of plausible salvage (a half-charged battery, a length of usable wire, a sealed container of clean water, a still-edible ration, a tool of one trade). It is what the place actually had.

Toxic-Lung Filters. You reroll the lowest die on checks against airborne poisons, toxic gas, and rad-dust. You can hold your breath for 10 minutes.

Bladed Tempo

Your weapons are punctuation.

Rules

When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you may immediately draw or stow a weapon, or shift 1 square without provoking reaction strikes.

✍ Table rule.

Level 3 — Null Field

Your blade suppresses their banked rerolls.

Mechanical Effects

When you hit a creature while at Burn 1+:

  • Suppress one of the following until the end of its next turn:

    • reroll the lowest die on attacks

    • Bonus damage

    • Fear or inspiration effects

At Burn 3+:

  • The target also loses reactions

Hope falters where you cut.

Bound and Bargained

A sealed pact holds itself; you need only keep the terms.

Rules

While your Sealed Pact stance is active, the bindings carry part of your will for you: your Clarity maximum rises by 1.

Requires: Pactkeeper⚙ Applies automatically while the Sealed Pact stance is active: Clarity max +1.

Level 6 — Silence of Will

You break focus.

  • Cannot benefit from rallying or command effects

At Burn 3+:

Hope stops organizing itself.

Adaptive Defense

Defense is not denial. It is management.

Rules

When you are hit by an attack you can see, you may use your reaction to reduce the damage by an amount equal to your rank bonus + your Violence or Intrigue value (your choice).

🃏 Card — click ▶ when you are hit: it shows the reduction (rank bonus + Violence or Intrigue).

Level 10 — Dread Cut

Fear propagates.

Mechanical Effects

When you hit at Burn 2+:

  • Target must make a defense check or be Shaken

  • Nearby enemies must make a defense check or suffer hesitation (lose movement or reactions)

At Burn 4+:

  • Fear spreads automatically to one additional creature

Dread is contagious.

Crew Type (Bad Eden): Mercenary Band.

“We are not a problem. We are a subscription.”

Mercenary Bands turn violence into a service industry. They’re disciplined when paid, unpredictable when not, and always looking for the next contract that lets them keep their code while breaking yours.

  • Tactical Identity: You gain a skill rank in Plating and Melee.
  • Strategic Identity: Your Domain earns +10 Violence marks each turn while you serve it.
